topics.title: Coursework
topics.summary: Adelaide’s coursework procedure says course coordinators must inform students about appropriate GenAI use in the course. It does not grant blanket permission for every assignment.

claims.text: For Adelaide University coursework assessment, the Assessment Procedure states that course coordinators will ensure students are informed about appropriate use of generative AI and similar tools in the course.

evidence.quote: The [Course Coordinator] will ensure students are informed about the standards associated with evidence-based academic writing, the appropriate use of generative artificial intelligence and similar tools, and relevant scholarly and/or professional conventions that apply to assessment in the course.
evidence.title: Assessment Procedure | Policies and Procedures | Adelaide University

claims.text: Adelaide University's invigilated online exam rules state that students may use only tools, software, or materials explicitly approved in exam instructions, and list AI tools such as ChatGPT as not permitted.

evidence.quote: Note: Anything not listed is prohibited. Use only tools, software, or materials explicitly approved in your exam instructions. This includes: No collaboration tools (email, forums, etc.); No additional electronic devices; No AI tools (e.g., ChatGPT); No physical items (pens, paper, calculators).

topics.title: Disclosure
topics.summary: Adelaide identifies unacknowledged AI-generated information as potentially inappropriate use. Graduate researchers also have specific recordkeeping and thesis/publication acknowledgement requirements.
topics.scope: These are Adelaide University references for the institution operating in 2026. Coursework, invigilated online exams and graduate research/publications have distinct rules; predecessor policies are not inherited here.

claims.text: Adelaide University's Academic Integrity Policy treats inappropriate use of AI that subverts an assignment or gives unfair academic advantage as an example of academic misconduct, including submitting AI-produced work as the student's own or using AI-generated information without acknowledgement.

evidence.quote: Inappropriate use of artificial intelligence (AI) - is to subvert the aims of assignment or give the student an unfair academic advantage. Inappropriate use of AI can include but is not limited to: submitting work produced (or produced in part) by generative artificial intelligence as the student's own work; using information generated by artificial intelligence without acknowledgement or attribution.
evidence.location: Definitions used in our policy - Academic Misconduct
evidence.title: Academic Integrity Policy | Policies and Procedures | Adelaide University

claims.text: Adelaide University's Graduate Research School guidance says graduate research students' use of generative AI must be transparent and responsible, including discussing use with a supervisor, keeping records, and acknowledging AI use in thesis acknowledgements, presentations, and publications.

evidence.quote: Generative AI tools generate new content such as text or images based on prompts from the user. These tools can support your research, but their use must be transparent and responsible. You must: discuss AI use with your supervisor; keep records of programs or applications used, dates and prompts; include an AI use statement in your thesis acknowledgements; acknowledge AI use in presentations and publications.
evidence.title: Conduct of research | Graduate Research School | Adelaide University

coursework.en: Adelaide’s coursework procedure says course coordinators must inform students about appropriate GenAI use in the course. It does not grant blanket permission for every assignment.
coursework.zh: Adelaide 的课程考核程序要求课程协调人向学生说明该课程中生成式 AI 的适当用法；这不代表所有作业一律获准使用。

exams.en: For Adelaide’s invigilated online exams, the retained rules require explicitly approved tools and list AI tools such as ChatGPT among prohibited items. Check your exam instructions.
exams.zh: Adelaide 的受监考在线考试规则要求只使用明确获批的工具，并将 ChatGPT 等 AI 工具列为禁止项目。请核对本场考试说明。

disclosure.en: Adelaide identifies unacknowledged AI-generated information as potentially inappropriate use. Graduate researchers also have specific recordkeeping and thesis/publication acknowledgement requirements.
disclosure.zh: Adelaide 将未注明来源的 AI 生成信息列为不当使用的可能情形；研究生研究另有使用记录和论文／发表致谢要求。

privacy_data.en: Adelaide Graduate Research School guidance tells graduate researchers not to upload sensitive, copyrighted or confidential information, or unprotected IP, into AI tools.
privacy_data.zh: Adelaide 研究生院指引要求研究生研究者不要向 AI 工具上传敏感、受版权保护、保密的信息或未受保护的知识产权内容。

approved_tools.en: The retained Adelaide tool records do not establish current account eligibility or costs. Institutional access is separate from course and exam permission.
approved_tools.zh: 保留的 Adelaide 工具记录未确立当前账户资格或费用；机构提供访问与课程、考试使用许可是不同事项。

research_publication.en: Adelaide graduate researchers must discuss AI use with supervisors, keep records and acknowledge use. The authorship procedure allows readability support, requires transparent disclosure and excludes AI authorship.
research_publication.zh: Adelaide 研究生研究者须与导师讨论 AI 使用、保留记录并作注明；作者署名程序允许以 AI 辅助提高可读性，要求透明披露，且不允许 AI 署名为作者。

academic_integrity.en: Adelaide’s policy identifies AI use that subverts an assignment or gives unfair advantage as misconduct, including passing AI-produced work off as one’s own. No general penalty is concluded here.
academic_integrity.zh: Adelaide 政策将破坏作业目标或取得不公平优势的 AI 使用列为学术违规，包括把 AI 生成作品冒作本人作品；此处不据此推定通用处分。

teaching_guidance.en: Adelaide course coordinators are responsible for informing students about appropriate GenAI use and relevant scholarly or professional conventions for the assessment.
teaching_guidance.zh: Adelaide 课程协调人负责向学生说明生成式 AI 的适当用法，以及该项考核适用的学术或专业惯例。

security_procurement.en: Adelaide’s Cyber Security Policy places AI systems under the same cyber security, data protection and compliance requirements as other information systems. It does not certify a particular tool.
security_procurement.zh: Adelaide《网络安全政策》要求 AI 系统遵守与其他信息系统相同的网络安全、数据保护和合规要求；这并非对某个工具的认证。

do.en: For Adelaide publications using GenAI, disclose its use transparently.

dont.en: Do not list generative AI as an author of an Adelaide publication.
dont.zh: 不要将生成式 AI 列为 Adelaide 学术发表的作者。

claim-adelaide-001.text: Adelaide University's Academic Integrity Policy treats inappropriate use of AI that subverts an assignment or gives unfair academic advantage as an example of academic misconduct, including submitting AI-produced work as the student's own or using AI-generated information without acknowledgement.
claim-adelaide-001.scope: Adelaide University operative in 2026 is distinct from its predecessors. Coursework integrity/assessment, invigilated online exams and graduate research/authorship rules have different audiences. Early Resolution is a limited procedure; no general sanction or appeal deadline is confirmed. Original public references remain pending currentness review.

evidence.quote: Inappropriate use of artificial intelligence (AI) - is to subvert the aims of assignment or give the student an unfair academic advantage. Inappropriate use of AI can include but is not limited to: submitting work produced (or produced in part) by generative artificial intelligence as the student's own work; using information generated by artificial intelligence without acknowledgement or attribution.
evidence.location: Definitions used in our policy - Academic Misconduct

claim-adelaide-007.text: Adelaide University's Authorship Procedure states that generative AI can be used to improve readability and clarity in publications, but must not be considered or listed as an author and its use must be disclosed transparently.
claim-adelaide-007.scope: Authorship/publication procedure; disclosure here is publication-specific.

evidence.quote: Generative AI can be used in publications to improve the readability and clarity of written content by assisting authors with generating drafts, revising language, and suggesting phrasing. Generative AI must not be considered an author itself, and its use must be disclosed transparently.

claim-adelaide-004.text: Adelaide University's invigilated online exam rules state that students may use only tools, software, or materials explicitly approved in exam instructions, and list AI tools such as ChatGPT as not permitted.
claim-adelaide-004.scope: Invigilated online exams and their approved exam instructions only; not every learning activity.

evidence.quote: Note: Anything not listed is prohibited. Use only tools, software, or materials explicitly approved in your exam instructions. This includes: No collaboration tools (email, forums, etc.); No additional electronic devices; No AI tools (e.g., ChatGPT); No physical items (pens, paper, calculators).

claim-adelaide-005.text: Adelaide University's Graduate Research School guidance says graduate research students' use of generative AI must be transparent and responsible, including discussing use with a supervisor, keeping records, and acknowledging AI use in thesis acknowledgements, presentations, and publications.
claim-adelaide-005.scope: Graduate Research School graduate-research guidance; do not apply as the coursework discipline procedure.

evidence.quote: Generative AI tools generate new content such as text or images based on prompts from the user. These tools can support your research, but their use must be transparent and responsible. You must: discuss AI use with your supervisor; keep records of programs or applications used, dates and prompts; include an AI use statement in your thesis acknowledgements; acknowledge AI use in presentations and publications.

claim-adelaide-006.text: Adelaide University's Graduate Research School guidance tells graduate research students not to upload sensitive, copyrighted, or confidential information, or unprotected intellectual property, into AI tools.
claim-adelaide-006.scope: Graduate research data/IP guidance; not a universal tool access determination.

evidence.quote: You must not: generate thesis content using AI (unless quoted and cited); translate large portions of text using AI; upload sensitive, copyrighted or confidential information into AI tools; upload unprotected intellectual property into AI tools.

claim-adelaide-008.text: Adelaide University's Cyber Security Policy states that AI systems are part of its digital environment and are subject to the same cyber security, data protection, and compliance requirements as other information systems.
claim-adelaide-008.scope: Adelaide University operative in 2026 is distinct from its predecessors. Coursework integrity/assessment, invigilated online exams and graduate research/authorship rules have different audiences. Early Resolution is a limited procedure; no general sanction or appeal deadline is confirmed. Original public references remain pending currentness review.

evidence.quote: Adelaide University recognises that artificial intelligence (AI) systems form part of its digital environment and are subject to the same cyber security, data protection, and compliance requirements as other information systems.
evidence.location: Section 3.2 - We apply secure and responsible practices to AI systems and data

claim-adelaide-003.text: For Adelaide University coursework assessment, the Assessment Procedure states that course coordinators will ensure students are informed about appropriate use of generative AI and similar tools in the course.
claim-adelaide-003.scope: Adelaide University operative in 2026 is distinct from its predecessors. Coursework integrity/assessment, invigilated online exams and graduate research/authorship rules have different audiences. Early Resolution is a limited procedure; no general sanction or appeal deadline is confirmed. Original public references remain pending currentness review.

evidence.quote: The [Course Coordinator] will ensure students are informed about the standards associated with evidence-based academic writing, the appropriate use of generative artificial intelligence and similar tools, and relevant scholarly and/or professional conventions that apply to assessment in the course.
